text:
alex: Quick heads-up — seeing low cross-request KV reuse even when requests share the same prompt prefix. repro on prod canary.

mira: Do you have hit-rate numbers? suspected fragmentation or key-mismatch?

alex: grabbed a 10m sample from one canary host:
```
kv_total_lookups: 1_200_000
kv_exact_prefix_hits: 86_000 (7.1%)
kv_similar_prefix_hits: 24_000 (2.0%)
kv_miss: 1_090_000 (90.9%)
avg_kv_value_size_bytes: 1_024
prefix_entropy_metric: 0.78
```
Most of those misses look like identical user prefixes but different cache keys.

jon: Hmm. Could be our fingerprinting salted by session id or ephemeral nonce. Are we hashing the whole request instead of canonical prefix?

alex: yep — current key = sha256(tenant_salt || session_id || prefix_bytes). suspect session_id shouldn't be in key for prefix reuse.

sam: But we added session_id for safety to avoid cross-session leaking KV between tenants. If we remove it we need a different isolation control.

mira: Agreed. Proposal: introduce a "bridgecache" concept — soft-shared prefix entries with tenant-aware ACLs. Keying would be primary: sha256(tenant_salt || prefix_canonical), secondary affinity token: session_id used only for local strong-affinity, not for global key. Bridge entries have TTL and an eviction tag requiring re-check that the model+version matches.

jon: Sketch of key layers:
- primary_key = sha256(tenant_salt || model_id || prefix_canonical)
- affinity_tag = session_id (attached metadata, not part of primary hash)
- stored_entry = {value, model_signature, last_seen, affinity_count}
- bridge_ttl = 30s (config)
This keeps tenant isolation but allows reuse across sessions in same tenant if model matches.

alex: early profile with a local patch (bridge_ttl=20s) shows: 
```
kv_total_lookups: 1_200_000
kv_primary_hits: 263_000 (21.9%)  <-- up from 7.1%
kv_bridge_hits: 112_000 (9.3%)
kv_miss: 825_000 (68.8%)
avg_latency_token_ms: 12.3 -> 10.2 (end-to-end gen)
mem_rss_delta_mb: +48 (bridge entries retained briefly)
```
That seems promising but we need to understand fragmentation + eviction behavior if bridge entries increase residency.

sam: Security check — if we allow cross-session reuse inside same tenant, ensure PII-free prefixes only. How are we canonicalizing prefix? We should run prefix sanitizer: strip probable PII patterns (emails, credit cards) before caching.

mira: Already have a sanitizer pass for prefix canonicalization in request pipeline; bridgecache must call it pre-hash. Also we should tag entries with a "sanitized=true" flag and skip bridging if sanitized==false.

jon: Eviction note: our LRU slabs are per-host and we currently evict by entry size. Bridge entries tend to be slightly larger due to metadata; need to cap metadata and consider a compacted representation to avoid page churn.

infra-bot: snapshot: host-17 kv-residency: 78k entries, avg_entry_size 1056 bytes, fragmentation_estimate 12.4%

alex: fragmentation is the big worry. When we allow soft sharing, we observed small bursts of memory growth in long-context flows (30s+). Might be due to many similar prefixes with tiny variations (whitespace, punctuation).

mira: Two mitigations: canonicalize whitespace/punctuation aggressively and use a prefix clustering heuristic — hash prefixes into buckets by n-gram overlap and only keep canonical representative per bucket for bridging. Cuts duplication at cost of some false negatives.

sam: Also consider adaptive bridge_ttl that decays quicker for high-churn tenant workloads. Could be per-tenant policy: high-privacy tenants can opt-out or set ttl=0.

jon: For rollout: implement flag gated by tenant and host-level canary. Add metric: bridge_share_ratio = bridge_hits / primary_hits. Target initial window: bridge_share_ratio between 0.2-0.6. Also monitor rss_growth_per_min and page-fault-rate.

liz: Ops: I'll coordinate a staged canary. Plan: enable bridgecache on 5% host fleet for non-PHI tenants, 30m test, then 25% if rss_growth < 5% and latency improves. Add alert for rss_growth_per_min > 10MB/min or fragmentation > 20%.

alex: Action items I can take: implement primary_key change, attach affinity_tag, wire TTL config, add metric bridge_share_ratio.

mira: I'll add sanitizer gating and n-gram clustering proto. jon can help with slab eviction tuning.

jon: Will prototype compact metadata layout and compaction pass on eviction. Also add unit tests around canonicalization.

sam: I'll do a short threat assessment. If we leak anything we need quick rollback path.

liz: I'll schedule the canary and update runbook for rollback.

alex: Sounds good. Will post initial PR link when ready. Thanks. :thumbsup:
